location_qualifier: representative point; the headquarters place is not named
current_activity: Army Blumentritt is created under OB Nordwest to hold the Weser from Hameln to the coast
notes: Event date: CMH The Last Offensive ch. 17 p. 385: "For defending the Weser from Hameln to the coast (a line already breached), Busch was to have a hastily created special force called Army Blumentritt"; CMH The Last Offensive ch. 19 p. 460: "the essentially makeshift force, Army Blumentritt, formed in early April as a component of OB NORDWEST". Event definition: the order of 6 April and CMH's "early April"; the army existed on paper before it had troops. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Northwest Germany (representative point at Bremen) with a precision of 50 km. Location approximate: a representative point at Bremen for the northern end of the Weser line; no headquarters place is named. Location support: CMH gives the Weser from Hameln to the coast as its line and names no headquarters. Commander: General der Infanterie Günther Blumentritt. Opponents: British Second Army.

location_qualifier: the area in front of Bremen
current_activity: Army Blumentritt makes a week-long stand in front of Bremen, with sailors as infantry; Bremen falls on 26 April
notes: Event date: CMH The Last Offensive ch. 19 p. 460: "Strengthened by sailors fighting as infantry, the Germans made a stand for a week in front of Bremen, but by nightfall of 26 April the British were in full control of the city". Event definition: the end of the stand on 26 April, after about a week. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Bremen with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: Bremen stands for the defended area in front of the city; the army headquarters is not placed. Location support: CMH names Bremen as the city defended. Commander: General der Infanterie Günther Blumentritt. Opponents: British Second Army.
